facts.raw_span: A 13-year-old boy presented with a 1-year history of pain and swelling around his right ankle
pain and swelling around his right ankle that had been gradually increasing in size
bony thickening over the lateral malleolus
the ankle and subtalar joints had a full range of motion
Complete blood count was within normal limits
erythrocyte sedimentation rate was 68 mm at the first hour
a submetaphyseal lytic lesion in the distal tibia with a well-defined sclerotic margin
a diagnosis of Brodie’s abscess was made
curettage was performed under spinal anesthesia via an anterior approach

concepts.why: The patient presented with a 1-year history of pain and swelling around the right ankle, and radiography revealed a submetaphyseal lytic lesion in the distal tibia with a well-defined sclerotic margin, consistent with Brodie's abscess.
The patient's elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate and the presence of a submetaphyseal lytic lesion suggest chronic osteomyelitis.
The patient's symptoms of pain and swelling around the ankle, along with a full range of motion in the ankle and subtalar joints, could be consistent with juvenile idiopathic arthritis.
The presence of a submetaphyseal lytic lesion in the distal tibia could suggest Ewing's sarcoma, although the patient's age and other symptoms make this less likely.
The patient's symptoms of pain and swelling around the ankle, along with the presence of a submetaphyseal lytic lesion, could be consistent with osteoid osteoma.

The patient's elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate and the presence of a submetaphyseal lytic lesion suggest septic arthritis, although the absence of other symptoms such as fever and joint effusion make this less likely.
The patient's symptoms of pain and swelling around the ankle, along with the presence of a submetaphyseal lytic lesion, could be consistent with chronic recurrent multifocal osteomyelitis.
The presence of a submetaphyseal lytic lesion in the distal tibia could suggest Langerhans cell histiocytosis, although the patient's age and other symptoms make this less likely.

rationales.F03: Bony thickening is more typical of bone lesions like Brodie's abscess and osteoid osteoma.
rationales.F06: Elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate is a non-specific marker of inflammation.
rationales.F07: A submetaphyseal lytic lesion with a well-defined sclerotic margin is characteristic of Brodie's abscess.
rationales.F08: The diagnosis of Brodie's abscess was made based on the clinical and radiological findings.
